diagnostic.prompt: A force acts along a rod toward its pivot. Does it turn the rod? Explain how you would find the moment arm, then calculate torque for a perpendicular 4 N force at 0.5 m.
diagnostic.response: The perpendicular 4 N force at 0.5 m gives 2 N m. A larger force must turn it more, even if it points through the pivot.

gap.misconception: A larger force always produces a larger turning effect, regardless of its line of action

references.activity: Open section 10.6. Draw the pivot and force line for equal radial and perpendicular pushes at the same distance. Predict which produces more turning effect before calculating. Mark each perpendicular moment arm, then use r F sin(theta) to check your prediction. Explain why force magnitude alone is insufficient. If the source is blocked, ask the tutor for an alternative; opening the link is not completion of the task.
references.followUp: After the learner returns, pose a fresh unaided problem comparing a smaller oblique force with a larger force whose line passes through the pivot. Use different magnitudes, distances and angles from earlier questions. Ask for a prediction, a sketch of the moment arm and a calculation without the source open. Collect the response before showing an answer or rubric. Assess both the numerical result and why the radial force has zero torque; reading completion is not mastery.
